Turn the sleep article (high search impressions, no clicks) into native content on every platform. Search phrase: does poor sleep increase appetite.

Why does food feel harder to manage after a bad night's sleep?

Short sleep disrupts ghrelin and leptin, the hormones that signal hunger and fullness. Cravings for sugar and carbohydrates get louder, and a tired brain makes more emotional decisions about food.

It is biology, not a lack of willpower. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, rest is treated as part of the work. Two places to start: keep the same sleep and wake times every day, weekends included, and put screens away 30 minutes before bed.

The full article is in the first comment.

How poor sleep increases appetite and cravings.

Short sleep disrupts ghrelin and leptin, the two hormones that signal hunger and fullness. That is why the day after a bad night feels so much harder around food. It is biology, not willpower.

Swipe for what changes and two places to start tonight. Save this for the next rough night.

Bariatric Counseling Center, San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

#SleepAndAppetite #EmotionalEating #BariatricCounseling #VirtualTherapyTexas

The 3 p.m. trip to the vending machine often starts at 11 p.m. the night before.

Short sleep disrupts ghrelin and leptin, the hormones that signal hunger and fullness. Cravings for sugar and carbohydrates go up, and a tired brain makes more emotional decisions about food.

For professionals running on five or six hours, this shows up as afternoon cravings and evening eating that feels out of proportion to the day. It usually gets labeled a discipline problem. It is a biology problem with a behavioral solution.

Two places to start: the same sleep and wake times every day, weekends included, and screens away 30 minutes before bed.

At the Bariatric Counseling Center, sleep is part of how we help people understand and modify their relationship with food.

Mental Illness Awareness Week (Oct 4 to 10). Positions eating as a mental health subject, which is BCC's whole premise, and lands the four pillars in Todd's written form.

See email for recommended edits from SH This is Mental Illness Awareness Week, and it is a good week to say something plainly: eating and mood are not separate subjects.

Stress, anxiety and low mood change how, when and why people eat. Eating that feels out of control feeds shame, and shame feeds the next hard day. Treating one side and ignoring the other rarely holds.

That is why the program at the Bariatric Counseling Center is built the way it is. Behavioral therapy. Dietary guidance. Culinary classes. Mindful movement. One program, not four.

Emotional eating and mental health are one conversation.

Stress, anxiety and low mood change how, when and why people eat. Care works better when it treats both sides together.

Swipe through, and share it with someone who needs to hear it this week.

Bariatric Counseling Center, San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

#MentalIllnessAwarenessWeek #EmotionalEating #BariatricCounseling #VirtualTherapyTexas

When you refer a patient, the referral should not disappear.

Our team coordinates care with referring medical providers and, at patient discharge, we give referring providers a detailed summary of the patient's experience during the time in our intensive outpatient program, including changes in assessment scores measuring nutritional quality of life, disordered eating, anxiety, and depression, among other metrics.

Progress notes are available as requested along the way.

The program can be standalone behavioral care for people with obesity, or in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medication that patients receive from their medical providers.

(What does "the drive" mean? -SH) Virtual treatment for binge eating and emotional eating, available anywhere in Texas. The Bariatric Counseling Center of San Antonio offers its Intensive Outpatient Program virtually throughout Texas, with the same team and the same schedule. The program runs about three months and roughly 30 sessions, meeting 2 to 3 times per week, with morning, evening and Saturday tracks. We accept most health insurances, and our claims are processed under mental health benefits. If the drive has been the obstacle, it does not have to be one.

Who is the right referral to the Bariatric Counseling Center?

We offer an innovative program designed to help people who struggle with weight-loss, obesity, binge eating, and chronic over-eating.

In practice that means pre and post bariatric surgery  patients, patients on weight loss medications, as well as patients for whom behavioral care is the whole plan. The program can be standalone behavioral care, or in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medication that patients receive from their medical providers.

It is an intensive outpatient program: about three months, roughly 30 sessions, meeting 2 to 3 times per week, available virtually throughout Texas.

Binge eating disorder treatment in San Antonio and virtually throughout Texas. Binge eating disorder is a recognized, treatable condition, not a failure of willpower. At the Bariatric Counseling Center of San Antonio, treatment is delivered through an Intensive Outpatient Program that provides group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes and movement education, led by an experienced and compassionate team of behavioral healthcare professionals. The program runs about three months and roughly 30 sessions. We accept most health insurances. Learn how treatment works.

Global Peer Support Celebration Day. Written for working professionals as prospective clients, per the standing note that LinkedIn education should speak to professionals.

Today is Global Peer Support Celebration Day, and it is a good day to question a habit most high performers share: handling everything alone.

People who are competent everywhere else in their lives often treat their relationship with food as a private project. Private projects do not get feedback, and they do not get company.

The claim BCC can make and the large eating disorder chains cannot: behavioral treatment alongside weight loss medication. 'Weight loss medications' only, never the drug class abbreviation.

Weight loss medications quiet the hunger signal. They do not teach the skill.

Patients on these medications often describe the same thing: the "food noise" drops, and for the first time there is room to work, to think, to breathe. What we do with that room determines what happens when the coverage changes or the prescription stops.

That work is behavioral: coping skills for stress and emotion, structure around meals, cooking, movement that is enjoyable enough to keep.

We do not prescribe. Our program can be standalone behavioral care for people with obesity, or can be in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medication that patients receive from their medical providers.

If you prescribe these medications, we would like to be the behavioral half of the plan.

Behavioral support for people taking weight loss medications, in San Antonio and virtually throughout Texas. Medication can quiet hunger. It does not teach the skills for managing stress, habits, and emotions around food, and those skills are what remain when a prescription changes or stops. Holiday theme for working professionals: Q4 workload plus the holiday calendar is when 'I'll deal with it in January' takes hold.

The fourth quarter is when busy people decide to deal with their health in January.

It makes sense on paper. Year end deadlines, travel, school events and a holiday calendar that starts in October leave no room for anything new. So the plan becomes: push through, start over on the 1st.

The trouble is what ten weeks of pushing through costs. Stress eating, skipped meals that turn into large evenings, and a January that starts further back than October did.

Starting smaller works better than starting later. One fixed meal a day. One boundary around the office food. One conversation with someone qualified to help.

Our program is in network with most health insurances and available virtually throughout Texas, with morning, evening and Saturday tracks built for people who work.

Same subject for a workplace audience: the office candy bowl.

The office candy bowl is not a character test.

Every October it fills up, and for a few weeks a lot of capable people run a private tally at their desks: "Walked past it twice: good. Took three on a deadline: bad". By Friday the tally has turned into a self-shaming verdict: "Guilty". 

The candy is not the interesting part. The interesting part is what the afternoon was like when the hand went into the bowl. Tired, behind, under pressure, unfed since 7 a.m. That is information, and it is far more useful than a verdict.

Most of what we teach at the Bariatric Counseling Center starts there: noticing what the urge is responding to, and answering that instead.

Our program is in network with most health insurances.
